L172: # DataView
L173: 
L174: Baseline
L175: 
L176: Widely available
L177: 
L178: *
L179: 
L180: This feature is well established and works across many devices and browser versions. It’s been available across browsers since July 2015.
L181: 
L182: * Some parts of this feature may have varying levels of support.
L183: 
L184:   * 【86†See full compatibility】
L185:   * 【87†Learn more】
L186: 
L187: The `DataView` view provides a low-level interface for reading and writing multiple number types in a binary 【88†`ArrayBuffer`】, without having to care about the platform's 【89†endianness】.
L188: ## In this article
L189: 
L190:   * 【90†Description】
L191:   * 【91†Constructor】
L192:   * 【92†Instance properties】

L199: ## 【90†Description】
L200: ### 【97†Endianness】
L201: 
L202: Multi-byte number formats are represented in memory differently depending on machine architecture — see 【89†Endianness】 for an explanation. `DataView` accessors provide explicit control of how data is accessed, regardless of the executing computer's endianness. For example, 【57†WebAssembly】 memory is always little-endian, so you should use `DataView` instead of typed arrays to read and write multi-byte values. See 【98†`WebAssembly.Memory`】 for an example.
L203: js
L204: 
L205:     `const littleEndian = (() => {
L206:       const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(2);
L207:       new DataView(buffer).setInt16(0, 256, true /* littleEndian */);
L208:       // Int16Array uses the platform's endianness.
L209:       return new Int16Array(buffer)[0] === 256;
L210:     })();
L211:     console.log(littleEndian); // true or false
L212:     `
L213: 
L214: Note: `DataView` defaults to big-endian read and write, but most platforms use little-endian.
L215: ## 【91†Constructor】
L216: 
L217: 【99†`DataView()`】
L218: 
L219: 
L220: Creates a new `DataView` object.
L221: ## 【92†Instance properties】
L222: 
L223: These properties are defined on `DataView.prototype` and shared by all `DataView` instances.
L224: 
L225: 【100†`DataView.prototype.buffer`】
L226: 
L227: 
L228: Returns the 【88†`ArrayBuffer`】 referenced by the `DataView`.
L229: 
L230: 【101†`DataView.prototype.byteLength`】
L231: 
L232: 
L233: Returns the length (in bytes) of the `DataView`.
L234: 
L235: 【102†`DataView.prototype.byteOffset`】
L236: 
L237: 
L238: Returns the offset (in bytes) of the `DataView` from the start of its 【88†`ArrayBuffer`】.
L239: 
L240: 【103†`DataView.prototype.constructor`】
L241: The constructor function that created the instance object. For `DataView` instances, the initial value is the 【99†`DataView`】 constructor.
L242: 
L243: 【104†`DataView.prototype[Symbol.toStringTag]`】
L244: 
L245: 
L246: The initial value of the 【105†`[Symbol.toStringTag]`】 property is the string `"DataView"`. This property is used in 【106†`Object.prototype.toString()`】.

L248: 
L249: 【107†`DataView.prototype.getBigInt64()`】
L250: 
L251: 
L252: Reads 8 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView` and interprets them as a 64-bit signed integer.
L253: 
L254: 【108†`DataView.prototype.getBigUint64()`】
L255: 
L256: 
L257: Reads 8 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView` and interprets them as a 64-bit unsigned integer.
L258: 
L259: 【109†`DataView.prototype.getFloat16()`】
L260: Reads 2 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView` and interprets them as a 16-bit floating point number.
L261:

L263:

L265: Reads 4 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView` and interprets them as a 32-bit floating point number.
L266: 
L267: 【111†`DataView.prototype.getFloat64()`】

L270: Reads 8 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView` and interprets them as a 64-bit floating point number.
L271: 【112†`DataView.prototype.getInt16()`】
L272:

L291: 
L292: 
L293: Reads 4 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView` and interprets them as a 32-bit unsigned integer.
L294: 
L295: 【117†`DataView.prototype.getUint8()`】
L296: 
L297:

L300:

L302: Takes a BigInt and stores it as a 64-bit signed integer in the 8 bytes starting at the specified byte offset of this `DataView`.
L303:

L309: 【120†`DataView.prototype.setFloat16()`】

L326:

L329:

L347: ## 【94†Examples】
L348: 
L349: ### 【129†Using DataView】
L350: 
L351: js
L352: 
L353:     `const buffer = new ArrayBuffer(16);
L354:     const view = new DataView(buffer, 0);
L355: 
L356:     view.setInt16(1, 42);
L357:     view.getInt16(1); // 42
L358:     `
L359:
